assertion_ids: A04 binding guidance is authoring metadata only
acceptance.given: The requirements input contains the implementation-binding section and A1–A4 grouping labels.

oracle.expected: A04's requirement and test contract explicitly check that binding metadata does not create product scope or published slice/evidence identities.
forbidden: Binding metadata is treated as new product scope.
A1–A4 labels are used as published slice IDs or evidence identities.
oracle.observable: An artifact/contract check of the frozen requirements and compiled plan confirms the binding section remains authoring guidance and A1–A4 labels are absent from published slice IDs and evidence identities.

acceptance.then: The artifact check passes only when binding metadata informs authoring without adding product scope or published identities.
acceptance.when: During plan contract review, inspect the binding section and compiled plan identity fields; evaluate this structural constraint before runtime execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A04 artifact/contract assertion detects when implementation-binding guidance is promoted into product scope or A1–A4 labels appear as published slice or evidence identities.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve the binding section as non-normative authoring metadata and keep A1–A4 out of published identity fields.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No runtime or schema state changes; restore the prior authoring-only interpretation if the contract check exposes a scope or identity leak.

slice_hint.state_transition: Binding guidance is interpreted as authoring metadata before compilation; compiled product scope and identities remain independent of A1–A4 labels.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A structural artifact check confirms the metadata adds no product scope and no A1–A4 published identities.

assertion_ids: Failure evidence is retained after local failure
Repair scope follows affected ownership and dependencies
Shared semantic change invalidates affected proofs
One terminal replay follows targeted stabilization with original binding identity
acceptance.given: A validation run has a local failure or a shared policy, schema, or validator semantic change, and the run has a recorded binding identity.

oracle.expected: Failure evidence remains available; repair targets only the affected group and dependents; shared semantic changes invalidate every affected proof; targeted checks stabilize before exactly one terminal replay using the original binding identity.
forbidden: Unrelated groups are repaired without cause.
Affected proofs remain current after shared semantic changes.
Terminal replay occurs before affected targeted checks stabilize.
Replay uses a different or rebuilt identity instead of first rebuilding the original binding identity.
oracle.observable: Lifecycle records show retained failure evidence, cause-bounded repair, invalidated affected proofs, stabilized targeted checks, and a terminal replay after rebuilding and reusing the same original binding identity.

acceptance.then: The lifecycle check passes when repair and proof invalidation follow the changed ownership/dependency boundary and one terminal replay occurs only after targeted stabilization with the original binding identity rebuilt and reused.
acceptance.when: During repair and terminal validation, evaluate the ordered lifecycle records and binding identity; replay obligations must rebuild the original binding identity before replaying with that same identity.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The lifecycle contract assertion fails if evidence is lost, repair exceeds affected ownership/dependencies, affected proofs remain current, or terminal replay precedes targeted stabilization or does not reuse the rebuilt original binding identity.

affected_subjects: Failure repair and proof invalidation lifecycle
slice_hint.behavior_change: Define ordered evidence retention, affected-scope repair, proof invalidation, targeted stabilization, and single terminal replay using the rebuilt original binding identity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted runtime/schema migration; retain historical failure evidence and restore the previous lifecycle contract if validation finds an ordering or identity violation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Local failures retain evidence and trigger bounded repair; shared semantic changes invalidate affected proofs; stabilized targeted checks precede one replay under the rebuilt original binding identity.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Lifecycle artifact checks establish retained evidence, affected-only repair and invalidation, targeted stabilization, and exactly one terminal replay using the rebuilt original binding identity.

acceptance.given: The declared Package A pytest modules and their test cases are authored according to the frozen SM-REPAIR-CONSTRAINTS test-authoring rule.

oracle.expected: Repository inspection and targeted pytest collection find one primary test named test_a01 through test_a25 for each intent, including the corresponding case for this obligation, and boundary variants expose explicit nonempty pytest parameter IDs.
forbidden: Any declared intent lacks its named primary test case.
Any boundary variant is collected without an explicit parameter ID.
oracle.observable: Pytest collection output and source inspection show the required per-intent test names and explicit parameter IDs.

acceptance.then: The per-intent selectors and boundary parameter IDs are mechanically discoverable in the authored test modules.
acceptance.when: Run selector and collection checks against the authored Package A test modules, evaluating test names and parameter IDs before implementation acceptance.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The targeted pytest collection/source check must fail when a required test_a01 through test_a25 selector is absent from its declared group test owner.
The targeted pytest collection/source check must fail when a boundary variant is declared without an explicit pytest parameter ID.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Author and verify the frozen per-intent pytest selectors test_a01 through test_a25 and explicit parameter IDs for boundary variants.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Remove only newly authored selector tests and helper fixtures; no production or schema state changes are involved.

slice_hint.state_transition: Declared test modules move from unauthored selectors to collected per-intent selectors with explicit boundary parameter IDs.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The four declared Package A pytest modules collect all required test_a01 through test_a25 selectors and explicit parameter IDs.

acceptance.given: The validator is invoked with the repository root, the declared normative policy path, a package root, and strict mode.

oracle.expected: The validator loads and applies rules from the supplied normative policy and schema files, so changing an applicable policy or schema rule changes the structured validation outcome; the result includes the declared versioned shape and authorizes is an empty array.
forbidden: The policy or schemas are unused parallel documentation.
Validation outcome remains unchanged when an applicable policy or schema rule is altered.
oracle.observable: An integration test runs the real validator entry with a temporary package and controlled policy/schema mutations, then compares structured status, diagnostics or rule identifiers, and authorizes from fresh JSON output.

acceptance.then: The validator consumes the normative policy and schemas as actual inputs and produces validation behavior driven by them.
acceptance.when: During validator execution and the integration test's controlled policy/schema mutation checks; the test evaluates the emitted structured result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_migration.py invokes the real validate_package entry or published CLI with literal arguments, mutates an applicable policy or schema rule, and raises AssertionError if the structured outcome does not change accordingly or authorizes is not [].

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make validate_package and the published CLI load the supplied normative policy and quality schemas and drive validation and result shaping from those inputs.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert validator and normative policy/schema changes together; preserve the existing result schema/version and callable API compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Policy and schema artifacts are authored as normative inputs; validator execution reads them and emits behavior and diagnostics determined by their contents.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The real validator integration selector passes when supplied policy/schema mutations alter the structured validation result as specified, and fails with an AssertionError when the validator ignores those inputs.
